findings.evidence: The 'Continue' button is a prominent red button while 'Never mind, take me back' is a plain text link, making the option to reverse the cancellation decision visually weaker than the option to proceed with the cancellation flow.
findings.explanation: The design makes it harder for users to easily reverse their decision to cancel by styling the 'take me back' option as a less prominent text link compared to the primary 'Continue' button.

findings.evidence: This offer expires in 00:59 countdown timer creates artificial time pressure to accept the offer before the user can make a considered decision about cancellation.
findings.explanation: The countdown timer pressures the user to make a quick decision about accepting the retention offer rather than proceeding with cancellation, which is a common dark pattern to prevent users from completing their intended action.

findings.evidence: The 'Continue' button is styled as a prominent red button while the 'Never mind, take me back' option is a plain text link, creating a visual hierarchy that emphasizes continuing the cancellation process over reversing the decision.
findings.explanation: The visual prominence of the 'Continue' button over the 'Never mind' option misdirects users toward continuing the cancellation process rather than easily reversing their decision, which is a misdirection pattern.

findings.evidence: The page requires users to answer 'What is the main reason you are leaving?' with radio button options before they can proceed with the cancellation process.
findings.explanation: This adds an unnecessary step to the cancellation process by forcing users to complete a survey before they can continue with their intended action of canceling the subscription.

findings.evidence: The checkbox 'Keep my profile and stay on Netflix Basic (free) — I understand my Premium plan will end' is pre-checked by default.
findings.explanation: The pre-selected checkbox favors the business by defaulting to a retention option, requiring the user to actively uncheck it to proceed with cancellation, which adds friction to the cancellation process.

legal.title: Résiliation en trois clics
legal.summary: Since 1 June 2023 (loi n° 2022-1158), a contract that can be concluded online must be cancellable online through a free, easily accessible feature.

legal.title: Simple mechanism to stop recurring charges
legal.summary: The Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act requires online negative-option sellers to provide simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges. (The FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel rule was vacated in July 2025; ROSCA still applies.)

legal.title: California Automatic Renewal Law
legal.summary: Consumers who sign up online must be able to cancel online, without obstruction.

legal.title: Ban on deceptive interface design by online platforms
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 forbids online platforms from designing interfaces that deceive or manipulate users, including giving more prominence to certain choices, repeatedly requesting a choice already made, and making termination harder than subscribing.

legal.title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
legal.summary: Prohibits misleading and aggressive commercial practices, including non-contractual barriers to terminating a contract.

legal.title: Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it
legal.summary: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 requires that it be as easy to withdraw consent as to give it.
